summary: This bill, titled the "Building Unrivaled Infrastructure and Long-term Development for America’s 250th Act" or the "BUILD America 250 Act," authorizes funding for federal-aid highways, bridge construction and rehabilitation, highway safety programs, transit programs, and rail programs for fiscal years 2027 through 2031, while also introducing reforms to project delivery, environmental review processes, and various transportation-related regulations.

scores.thoughts: This bill is primarily focused on authorizing significant appropriations from the Highway Trust Fund and the general fund for various transportation programs, including federal-aid highways, bridges, public transportation, highway safety, and rail programs, for fiscal years 2027 through 2031. It explicitly details billions of dollars in authorized spending across numerous sub-programs, indicating a substantial increase in government spending on infrastructure.

The bill is a multi-year surface transportation reauthorization that authorizes tens of billions in new spending from the Highway Trust Fund and general revenues for highways, bridges, transit, rail, safety, and related programs (FY 2027–2031). It contains no offsetting revenue measures or spending reductions. A vote on the bill is therefore a vote to increase outlays without corresponding deficit reduction, pushing the measure toward the -1 end of the spectrum. While infrastructure investment is the bill’s central purpose, the scale of new authorizations gives the deficit impact moderate centrality to the legislation as a whole.
